# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-14 (Extended v115)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Summer Year 4, transitioning to winter)**: Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon; le Petit-Picpus convent district; M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens (Rue de l'Ouest side); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Staveford, Gulhaven); Wilwick; Sceaux (ball location); Père-Lachaise cemetery; harbor town of Dunstead. **Environmental progression**: Spring—frost silvering hedges, light early, smoke flat; Summer—warm air, sparrows chirping, bees humming in lavender, gulls quarrying, salt and tar scent from water, wind off water carries salt and tar, chimneys smoking flat, evening light early; **Autumn/Winter transition**: icy breeze through windows, snow falling, Candlemas sun promising snow that arrives, outer mist penetrating like whitish wadding, bell for vespers ringing thinly.

## Primary Locations
**LUXEMBOURG GARDENS**: Fountain basin with swans; statues including Leonidas, Spartacus, Gladiator; "his alley" on Rue de l'Ouest side with recurring bench; bench by Gladiator near other end. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus convent. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet, 30 francs annually. **JONDRETTE DEN** (Summer Year 4): Unidentified location within or near Gorbeau house; abject, dirty, fetid, sordid; furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets; dormer window four panes draped in spiders' webs; leprous walls with seams and scars; obscene sketches in charcoal; repulsive moisture; let for forty francs yearly; floor uneven, antique plaster blackened; fireplace with brazier, pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage, ashes. **Architectural features**: Attic large with projections, angles, black holes, bays, promontories; horrible unfathomable nooks suggesting spiders large as fist, wood-lice large as foot, possibly monstrous human beings hiding. One pallet near door, one near window. Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (black frame) suspended on nail: sleeping woman and child, eagle in cloud with crown, woman thrusting crown away, Napoleon in glory on blue column with yellow capital. Wooden panel (longer than broad) stood on ground against wall, picture-face turned to wall, like pier-glass forgotten awaiting rehang. Windows with broken panes. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; thatched cottage; fifty crowns yearly; three rooms, enclosed garden.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as assistant gardener in convent; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. Nuns unaware of circumstances.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. **Status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps around Gorbeau house; confident convict nearby.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development and Melancholy

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old (Spring Year 4); three years since left grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen; believes grandfather burned it.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 calmed views. Sympathies to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed, poet over hero. Preferred introspection to action.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually; daily sustenance 20 sous (365 francs yearly); clothing 100 francs; linen/washing 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. Earned approximately seven hundred francs yearly. **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered fifteen hundred francs yearly—Marius refused to preserve liberty and dignity. Deliberately stopped working to dedicate time to thought and meditation.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent estrangement three years ago without rapprochement—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends. Did not enter decidedly into group but remained cordial. Close to **M. Mabeuf**—owed him revolution within soul; indebted for knowing and loving his father. **Recent social activities (Spring Year 4)**: Dined with Courfeyrac; breakfasted at Café Voltaire.

## The Mysterious Couple and Marius's Passion Cycle

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty (M. Leblanc) and very young girl (thirteen/fourteen) on Luxembourg bench daily. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly; wore blue trousers and coat, broad-brimmed hat, black cravat, white shirt, white hair. Girl: thin, awkward, promise of handsome eyes; wore convent scholar dress.

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased for unknown reason.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Girl became well-dressed young maiden. Wore black damask dress and cape, white crape bonnet, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe.

**Marius's indifference (Summer Year 3)**: When she raised eyelids, Marius found only child's glance. She looked indifferently. Marius paid no further attention.

**First meaningful glance and awakening (Spring Year 4)**: On warm day in Luxembourg, their glances met. Marius perceived he wore everyday clothes; resolved to dress differently. Following day wore new coat, seated himself surveying her. Left only when gates closed. His worship of his father retreated to depths of soul.

**Marius's emotional transformation**: Love came. Brain felt on fire. She appeared beautiful, wholly feminine and angelic. Seemed floating free in azure heavens. Vexed about dust on boots. Followed her with eyes until disappeared. Walked like madman; ate and spoke excitedly; laughed uproariously.

**Strategic approach (Spring Year 4)**: Combined stations behind trees and pedestals with diplomacy to be seen by girl and unseen by M. Leblanc. Sometimes remained motionless half-hour in shade. She bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye.

**M. Leblanc's response**: Noticed something. Often rose when Marius arrived and moved to bench by Gladiator near other end. Marius did not pursue. M. Leblanc made daughter pass carriage entrance first, then stared intently at Marius.

**Escalation and handkerchief (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench after they left. Very simple, white, fine, exhaled ineffable perfume. Marked with letters U. F. Marius immediately thought "Ursule!" Kissed handkerchief, placed on heart during day; laid beneath lips at night.

**Leg incident and jealousy (Spring Year 4)**: Brisk May breeze lifted dress to height of garter. **A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius saw it. He was exasperated and furious.** Girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. Marius determined to be vexed. **Harsh and capricious jealousy of the flesh awakened in his heart.** When she passed bench, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance. She gave slight straightening up with backward movement: "Well, what is the matter?"

**Veteran encounter and paroxysm**: A bent, wrinkled, pale veteran in Louis XV uniform bearing soldier's cross of Saint-Louis crossed walk. Marius thought he perceived man had extremely well satisfied air; struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal and merry wink. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!" Felt desire to exterminate the veteran.

**M. Leblanc and girl's disappearance (Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Summer passed, autumn came, winter arrived. Neither set foot in Luxembourg garden again. **Marius had but one thought—to gaze once more on that sweet and adorable face.** Fell into black melancholy. All was over. Work disgusted him; walking tired him. Everything had disappeared.

**Self-reproach (Autumn Year 4)**: Heaped hundred reproaches on himself: "Why did I follow her? I was happy at mere sight! Why wish to have more?" Confided nothing to Courfeyrac, but Courfeyrac guessed everything.

**Ball at Sceaux (September Year 4)**: Allowed himself taken to ball hoping to find her. Did not see her. Left friends and returned home on foot alone through night, weary, feverish, with sad and troubled eyes.

## The Jondrette Family and Daughters

**First girl's appearance and condition (Spring Year 4, morning)**: About seven o'clock, very young girl stood in half-open door. **She was frail, emaciated, slender creature**: nothing but chemise and petticoat on chilled, shivering nakedness. Girdle and head ribbon strings. Pointed shoulders, blond lymphatic pallor, earth-colored collar-bones, red hands, half-open degraded mouth missing teeth, dull bold base eyes. **Form of young girl who missed her youth; look of corrupt old woman; fifty years mingled with fifteen.** One of those beings both feeble and horrible. Most heart-breaking: in early childhood must have been pretty. Grace of her age struggling against hideous premature decrepitude. Remains of beauty dying away like pale sunlight extinguished under hideous clouds at dawn on winter day.

**Behavior in Marius's room (Spring Year 4)**: Entered resolutely, staring with assurance at whole room and unmade bed. Feet bare. Large holes in petticoat permitted glimpses of long legs and thin knees. Shivering. Without permission wandered back and forth with audacity of spectre. Kicked about without troubling herself. Occasionally chemise, untied and torn, fell almost to waist. Moved chairs, disarranged toilet articles, handled Marius's clothes, rummaged in corners.

**Marius's recognition**: Marius recognized his neighbor Jondrette, in distress, exercising industry of speculating on charity of benevolent persons. Procured addresses and wrote under feigned names to people judged wealthy and compassionate. His daughters delivered letters at their risk and peril. **Judging from girls' flight, breathless condition, terror, overheard slang, these unfortunate creatures were plying some inexplicably sad profession.** Result: two miserable beings—neither girls nor women—species of impure and innocent monsters produced by misery. **Sad creatures without name, sex, or age; to whom neither good nor evil any longer possible.** Blossomed out yesterday; faded today, like flowers let fall in streets, soiled with every sort of mire, waiting for some wheel to crush them.

**Second girl's appearance (Summer Year 4, later)**: Eldest girl entered after bursting door open abruptly. On feet: large coarse men's shoes bespattered with mud splashed to red ankles. Wrapped in old mantle hanging in tatters (probably deposited at door an hour previously to inspire pity, then picked up again on emerging). Completely breathless, took breath on pausing. Had been at church. Found man (M. Leblanc) in usual place. Made reverence, handed him letter. He read it, asked "Where do you live, my child?" She answered she would show him. He said no, requested address—his daughter had purchases to make, he would take carriage, reach house at same time. She gave address. When she mentioned house, he seemed surprised, hesitated instant, then said: "Never mind, I will come." After mass, she watched him leave church with daughter, saw them enter carriage. **Reported to father she told man last door in corridor, on right.**

**Second girl's complaints and refusal (Summer Year 4, later)**: She was clad only in chemise and knitted petticoat patched with old cloth. Coarse linen apron concealed half of petticoat. Although doubled up and bent together, she was of very lofty stature—sort of giant beside her husband (Jondrette). Hideous hair, reddish blond turning gray, thrust back from time to time with enormous shining hands, flat nails. Expressed refusal to wear shoes again: "I won't put these shoes on again, and that I won't, for the sake of my health, in the first place, and for the sake of cleanliness, in the next. I don't know anything more irritating than shoes that squelch, and go _ghi, ghi, ghi,_ the whole time. I prefer to go barefoot."

**Family dynamics (Summer Year 4)**: Marius gazed at this gloomy interior, more terrifying than tomb, for human soul could be felt fluttering there, life palpitating there. **Garret, cellar, lowly ditch where indigent wretches crawl at bottom of social edifice is not sepulchre but its antechamber; death places its greatest miseries in that vestibule.** **Bodies press close in misery, as in cold, but hearts draw apart.** Woman must have loved this man, judging from amount of love within her; but probably in daily reciprocal reproaches of horrible distress weighing on whole group, this had become extinct. Nothing more remained than ashes of affection. Caressing appellations survived: "_My dear, my little friend, my good man_," etc., with mouth while heart was silent.

## Friends of the A B C, Patron-Minette, and Criminal Underground

**Friends of the A B C**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people). Secret society in embryonic state. Meetings back room Café Musain. Members: Enjolras, Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students; cordial with working classes.

**Philosophical discourse on social substructure**: All human societies have subterranean dimensions. Encyclopedia in last century was open mine. Beneath social construction: religious, philosophical, economic, revolutionary mines. **Descending scale of toilers**: John Huss → Luther → Descartes → Voltaire → Condorcet → Robespierre → Marat → Babeuf. Common mark: disinterestedness.

**The third lower floor (_le troisième dessous_)**: Below all mines, below Babeuf, lies deepest stratum—**grave of shadows, cellar of blind, _Inferi_.** Wild spectres roam here, almost beasts, almost phantoms, unconcerned with universal progress. Occupied only with individual desires. Two step-mothers: ignorance and misery. Guide: necessity. Satisfaction: appetite. Brutally voracious—ferocious as tiger. From suffering pass to crime. Man becomes dragon. From this vault Lacenaire emerges. Object: destruction of everything. Desire: chaos. Vault formed of ignorance. **All others above have one object—suppress it.** So long as society remains what it is, they remain what they are. Individuals extirpated, tribe subsists.

**Patron-Minette: Criminal association**: Members Babet, Gueulemer, Claquesous, Montparnasse. **Gueulemer**: Six feet high, Hercules of no defined position. Lair: sewer of Arche-Marion. Pectoral muscles of marble, biceps of brass. Less than forty but crow's-feet, harsh short hair, cheeks like brush, beard like wild boar. Assassin through coolness. Possibly involved with Marshal Brune; porter at Avignon in 1815. After, turned ruffian. **Claquesous**: He was night. Emerged from hole at nightfall, returned before daylight. Hole location unknown. Addressed accomplices only in absolute darkness, back turned. Perhaps not named Claquesous; sobriquet only. If candle brought, put on mask. Ventriloquist. Never seen without mask. **Function**: Four ruffians formed Proteus, winding like serpent among police. Charged with general enterprise of ambushes in Seine department. Furnish canvas; undertake preparation of scenery. Kept troupe of shadow actors at disposition of underground tragedies. **Designation**: Name bestowed in subterranean circulation. In fantastic ancient popular parlance, _Patron-Minette_ signifies morning, as _entre chien et loup_ signifies evening. Probably derived from hour work ended, dawn vanishing moment for phantoms.

## English Provincial Towns: Movements and Incidents

**Population movements**: Rozek Stenenridge rode out of Dungate; living in Wilwick by next market day. Yera Haskick (Dunstead → Kelmere); Rinelle (Kelford → Torton); Kadrek Brackick (followed to Torton). Luena Stenenridge followed him to Wilwick within month. **Deaths**: Luwyn Brackick died of kick from cart horse; laid in churchyard at Dunstead. **Births**: Ferald and Isvie Stenworth (Dunstead, parents Luwyn Brackick); Zavus Prydenridge (Ostcombe, parents Wenelle and Rovus); Bremira Corrford (daughter of Kassa Brackick and Ulrald Corrford, Dunstead).

**Claims and rumors**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (claim—**later confirmed by Lurald telling Ulrald Corrford**). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). Granary fire set on purpose (rumor—**confirmed: Luena Stenenridge confided to Rozek that Dunstead granary fire was set on purpose**). Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Kassa Brackick confided mill ledger rewritten. Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family (claim—**later Fenelle told Peten Haskick this**). Price of salt scandal discussed. 

**Current incidents (Spring-Summer Year 4)**: Lura Haskick laughed at story nobody else found funny. Ferald Stenworth complained of aching back, as usual. Dog barked at nothing then went quiet. Ferald hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Argued with carter over oats price. Lura told Fenelle "You look tired"; Fenelle did not deny it. Luena watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly. Bremira fell asleep before fire. Thizek read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints. Conversations about weather, harvest, lame horse. Various characters laughed, argued, watched, remarked. Nerine, Rovus, Isric, Gadrek, Havie, Yedan, Vesmira also engaged in similar mundane activities. Isric gave up being smith and took work as glazier. Bought and regretted ribbon. Nerine counted coins twice, came up penny short.
